    Is it hard to get into Queens university?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    Queen's University in Canada is considered selective, with competitive admission requiring high academic standing, often an 80% to 90%+ average depending on the program
    . Top programs like Commerce and Health Sciences are extremely competitive, requiring averages in the low-to-mid 90s, while general arts/science programs often require low-to-mid 80s. 
    Key Takeaways on Admission Difficulty: 
    • Highly Competitive Programs: The Smith School of Business (Commerce) and Health Sciences/Nursing programs require top-tier grades, often 90% or higher.
    • General Admission: While the minimum threshold for some programs may be lower, a safe competitive average for many programs is in the high 80s to low 90s.
    • Academic Focus:
      Admission is primarily based on academic performance in high school, especially in senior-level courses.
    • Supplemental Information: Some specialized programs may require supplementary applications or interviews. 
    Note: The results regarding "Queens University" primarily reflect the competitive Canadian institution in Kingston, ON. If you meant Queens University of Charlotte, its admission is less competitive, with average SAT scores around 1130.

      Is Queens College an all-girls school?
      In the 1940s, we began our journey to become co-ed. Shortly after World War II men could attend Queens College, but could not live on campus. In 1948, Queens opened a co-ed evening college. In 1987, Queens made the decision to become co-ed, and the first residential male students were admitted in 1988.
